questions.explain: `stops[-1]` is the last item, so `stops[-2]` is the one before it: Park. The slice `stops[1:3]` takes index 1 and index 2. The trap is the stop value: index 3 is **not** included, so the slice has two items.

questions.code:
queue = [5, 9, 2, 9]
queue.remove(9)
queue.insert(1, 7)
last = queue.pop()
print(queue, last)
questions.explain: `remove(9)` takes out only the **first** 9, which gives `[5, 2, 9]`. `insert(1, 7)` puts 7 at index 1: `[5, 7, 2, 9]`. `pop()` takes out the last item and returns it, so `last` is 9. The trap is to think that `remove` deletes every 9.

`append` changes the list and returns `None`. The second line stores that `None` in `stops`, so the list is lost. The trap is to expect `append` to give the longer list back. Write `stops.append("Zoo")` on a line of its own.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with an index, so that the code prints the last item of the list. It must also work when the list gets longer or shorter.
questions.explain: `stops[-1]` is always the last item, and `stops[len(stops) - 1]` is the same item. The trap is `stops[len(stops)]`: indexes start at 0, so that position does not exist and Python raises an `IndexError`.
